payload.acceptance_criteria: - When a record waits on a cancelled or missing blocker, the tracker list shall say that blocker still holds it and not count it as done.
payload.description:
## Context

linksLine in .basicly/core/kit/board/web/index.html (line 416) counts every blocks target that is not in state.records as done. state.records holds only records that are not closed, so a cancelled blocker and a missing blocker both read as blocker done. Readiness (kit/tracker/derivation.py is_ready, lines 186-190) keeps a record held by a cancelled or missing blocker, so the list tells a reader a record is unblocked when the tracker will not start it. Found 2026-10-29 by the design review for basicly-tpr4xre.
payload.title: The tracker list says blocker done for a cancelled or missing blocker

payload.text: [design proposal 2026-10-29, designer agent, read-only] Recommended: Option A, an epic path line above the title plus a WAITS ON / UNBLOCKS block above Context, with a Show chain tree down to the blocker that can start now; then Option C, an epic map that lays out an epic's children in waves (topological over blocks, rank within a wave), no drawn lines, at #/record/<id>/map. Rejected: a three-column view (titles cut to 18 chars, stacks into A below 900 px) and a whole-ledger graph (largest component 845 of 1,810 records). Measured on this ledger: parent chains at most 3 deep, 2 records with two parents, at most 109 children, 0 cycles, 0 missing targets. API additions: issue_type and close_resolution on linked records and an ancestors list in record_view._edges; status on summary edges in queries._edges_of. Open questions for the owner: show what a story's epic waits on (rec: yes, muted, says it does not hold the story); show that an epic waits on its open children (rec: yes); map as a mode of the epic (rec: yes); compute ancestors on the server (rec: yes).
